historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic packaging growth (flat-to-low-single-digit volumes plus price/mix); every historical CAGR is dominated by the 30-Apr-2025 all-stock Berry merger
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (42.3% 3yr / 19.6% 5yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (16.9% / 12.8%) and EPS (-12.3% / -4.6%, split-normalised). Cause: Berry was paid for with ~846m (pre-split) new shares issued well above book, inflating equity without per-share earnings accretion. None of these CAGRs is usable as a forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (OCF - capex + disposals - SBC): FY2021 $961m, FY2023 $711m, FY2026 $1,219m. The owner-FCF CAGR sits within 0.3pp of the reported CAGR (SBC is only ~0.35% of revenue), so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. EPS normalised to post-split basis (pre-FY2024 EPS x5): FY2021 $3.01, FY2023 $3.53, FY2026 $2.38 GAAP (adjusted $4.02).

scenario_narratives.base: Berry integration lands roughly on plan: synergies reach the $650m run-rate by FY2028 but about 40% of the increment is passed back to large CPG customers in contract renewals, so all-in EBITDA margin climbs from ~14.8% (after integration cash) to 17.0% as restructuring spend rolls off. Volumes stay flat-to-low-single-digit (the Q4 FY2026 inflection is modest), revenue grows 2-3% on price/mix and healthcare/protein mix shift. The North American beverage sale/JV is assumed value-neutral. Capex holds at ~4% of sales and leverage drifts from ~3.5x toward the ~3x target through EBITDA growth rather than equity issuance.
scenario_narratives.bull: Synergies beat the $650m target and are largely retained, healthcare/pharma and protein flexibles mix lifts margins to ~18.3%, volumes recover to 1-2% on top of price, and the one-time ~$280m working-capital synergy plus the reversal of the FY2026 Middle-East inventory build lighten working-capital drag. A clean NA beverage exit removes a low-margin, capital-hungry drag. This is the path toward management's >$3bn FCF aspiration, and it needs several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: Integration slips: synergy capture stalls near the FY2026 ~$250m level and is competed away by regional flexible/rigid players, restructuring cash persists, consumer-staples volumes stay soft with private-label and destocking pressure, and PPWR/EPR costs are only partly passed through with the 3-6 month resin lag. EBITDA margin stalls at ~15.5%, capex runs higher for recyclability retooling, and growth is 0.5-2%. With 3.5x leverage there is no solvency event, but deleveraging stalls and the dividend absorbs most free cash flow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Amcor post-Berry is a scaled, defensive, low-growth packaging converter whose value rests on capturing merger synergies and converting them to cash while deleveraging. The model charges the integration cash the company excludes from adjusted figures, gives no tax credit for non-deductible acquired-intangible amortisation, and treats the headline '>$3bn FCF' target as a bull marker rather than an anchor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Synergy retention: every 1pp of EBITDA margin is ~$235m of EBITDA on FY2026 revenue
Leverage (~$12.9bn net debt) makes equity value highly geared to EV: a 1x EBITDA multiple move is ~$8/share
Terminal value is capped at 12-15x unlevered FCF (~7-9x EBITDA, in line with packaging peers); an uncapped Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would be ~20x
NA beverage divestiture could be dilutive if sold below the group multiple
Plastics regulation (EU PPWR, EPR fees) raising capex and cost
Fiscal-year change: the Jul-Dec 2026 Transition Period makes year-1 comparisons non-standard

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 36.25-50.94
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1748790), FY2026 10-K filed 2026-08-12; AMCR_Metrics.csv from core_metrics
data_sources.qualitative: AMCR_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): FY2026 results, Transition Period guidance adj EPS $1.80-1.90, leverage 3.5-3.6x by Dec-2026, $650m synergy target by FY2028

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares FY2026 (Q4 and full-year both 463.8m, post 1-for-5 reverse split of 14-Jan-2026); basic shares on the FY2026 10-K cover 462.3m (12-Aug-2026). Held FLAT: SBC expensed in the flows. No non-SBC issuance modelled; the ~846m (pre-split) Berry consideration shares are already in the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $83m (XBRL). Amcor settles awards partly with on-market treasury purchases ($29m FY2026), which is the mechanism keeping the count flat rather than an extra cost, so not added on top.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 30 June (changing to 31 December: Jul-Dec 2026 is a six-month Transition Period, first calendar fiscal year CY2027)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.05 (defensive packaging end-markets but 3.5x net debt/EBITDA) -> CoE ~9.5%. Pre-tax Kd ~5.0% (FY2026 interest expense $676m on ~$13.9bn average debt, new EUR/USD issues 2025-26) -> 3.95% after 21% tax. Market weights E ~$19.5bn / D ~$12.9bn (60/40) -> 7.3%; rounded up to 7.5%. Same WACC in all scenarios: integration and leverage risk is carried in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost ($289m FY2026) sits inside EBITDA and therefore inside the flows; operating lease liabilities ($1,068m) are NOT in net debt. Finance leases ($44m) are inside reported debt. One treatment, lease charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $11m of equity with $0m FY2026 NCI income; deducted once in the equity bridge at book.
inputs.debt_detail: Total debt = long-term debt incl. current maturities and finance leases $13,877m + short-term borrowings $135m = $14,012m; cash $1,115m; net debt $12,897m at 30-Jun-2026 (company-reported ~$12.9bn).
inputs.fcf_definition: Reported FCF = OCF $2,151m - capex $922m + PP&E disposal proceeds $73m = $1,302m (FY2026, after ~$611m cash interest, ~$215m restructuring and ~$220m Berry integration/transaction cash, and a Middle-East-related inventory build). Owner FCF = $1,302m - SBC $83m = $1,219m. Interest income ($66m) NOT stripped: the company is net debt, not net cash.
inputs.per_share_normalisation: Metrics.csv per-share history is mixed-basis: FY2024 onward rescaled to post-split (288.1m shares, EPS 2.52), FY2023 and earlier still pre-split (1,476m shares, EPS 0.705). For CAGRs, pre-FY2024 EPS multiplied by 5 and shares divided by 5. FY2025 318.6m is a full-year weighted average straddling the 30-Apr-2025 Berry close, not a period-end count.
inputs.period_alignment: FY0 = 12 months to 30-Jun-2026. Year 1 = 12 months to 30-Jun-2027 (the Jul-Dec 2026 Transition Period plus H1 CY2027); the calendar change relabels periods, it does not change annual cash generation, so projections stay on 12-month steps from the June anchor with end-of-year discounting.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, industrial/consumer packaging, US GAAP, USD). Not a bank/REIT/holdco; no live deal. No prior DCF or MEMORY entry, so this is a fresh build. EBITDA margin path is ADJUSTED EBITDA + SBC (pre-SBC; FY2026 adj EBITDA $3,673m + $83m = 16.0%) LESS the cash integration/restructuring charges management excludes (~1.2pp FY2026, rolling off by FY2029) -- so those costs are charged in the flows, not ignored. D&A path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (~$902m, 3.8%): the $577m amortisation of acquired intangibles (mostly Berry, an all-stock deal with no tax step-up) gives no cash tax shield, so it is left out of the tax base; the 21% cash rate on unlevered EBITA reconciles to FY2026 cash tax $451m plus the ~$130m interest shield the WACC already credits. Working capital capture -10% of revenue change (manufacturer: receivables + inventory > payables). Buybacks are negligible ($1m FY2026): the flat count is a modelling convention funded only by small treasury purchases for award settlement. Management's '>$3bn FCF by FY2028' target could not be reconciled with $3.7bn adjusted EBITDA less ~$1bn capex, ~$0.6bn interest and ~$0.6bn tax even at full $650m synergies (~$2.2-2.4bn); it is treated as a bull-case marker, not an anchor.

base.margin_rationale: FY2026 pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA 16.0% less ~1.2pp cash integration/restructuring = ~14.8% all-in. Base nets ~60% of the remaining ~$400m synergy ramp (to $650m run-rate by FY2028) after price give-backs to customers, and integration cash rolls off by FY2029 -> 17.0% mature, ~1pp above FY2026 adjusted.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 gross capex 3.9% of revenue (net of disposals 3.6%); legacy Amcor 3.4-3.9%. 4.0% allows for NA flexibles capacity and PPWR recyclability retooling.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): a thesis resting on merger-synergy execution while carrying ~3.5x net debt/EBITDA, with FY2026 FCF already guided down once. Base 50%: synergies are tracking ~10% ahead of the FY2026 plan. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs synergy retention, volume recovery and a clean NA beverage exit simultaneously.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
